Check the Sharing Labels That a Constructor Was Given

Source: R/hyper.R
check_ids.Rd

Validates id and returns it as a named character vector, one entry per hyperparameter to share, empty where the constructor was given none.

Usage

check_ids(x, names, what = "this term")

Arguments

x

The id argument as given: NULL, a single string, or a named character vector.

names

The hyperparameter names that the term's penalty carries, against which the names of the labels are checked, or NULL where the penalty does not exist yet. In that case the shape is checked and the labels are carried as written, to be resolved by a second call where the names are known.

what

How to name the term in a message.

Value

A character vector, possibly empty, named by the hyperparameters. In the deferred case (names = NULL) a single unnamed string is returned unnamed, to be named by the second call.

Details

Two forms are accepted and both have the same meaning. An unnamed single string shares the hyperparameter, and is valid only where the penalty carries one: it is the short form for the frequent case, a smooth or a ridge. A named vector, c(alpha = "A"), names the hyperparameter to share, and a penalty carrying several requires this form, since sharing the mixing of an elastic net while leaving its strength free is a different model from the reverse, and the code does not infer which one was meant.

The short form on a penalty carrying several hyperparameters is an error that lists them. The names are checked against the penalty's own, so a misspelling is reported where it was written.

Sharing does not merge the penalties. They remain two objects estimated at one value, and the code does not check whether they are comparable: the two may weigh quite different matrices, and whether that is the intended model is left to the caller. A shared value is most meaningful between penalties of the same shape over covariates of comparable scale.

See also

term_ids(), which reports it; check_hyper() for the argument that holds a hyperparameter instead of sharing it.
